The change is complete and the build is green.

## What I did

The business-day rule lived in `BusinessDay.rollForward(...)` (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/BusinessDay.java`), which only skipped weekends and jumped straight to the next Monday. I extended it to also skip the five fixed public holidays:

- Added a `HOLIDAYS` constant (2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28).
- Replaced the single Saturday/Sunday → Monday jump with a loop that rolls forward one day at a time until it lands on a genuine business day. This correctly handles the cascade case where the next day after a weekend is itself a holiday (e.g. 2026-12-25 is a Friday holiday → Sat/Sun → the following Monday, and 2026-12-28 is also a listed holiday, so it rolls on to 2026-12-29).
- Factored the day-of-week + holiday check into a small private `isBusinessDay(...)` helper so `rollForward` stays a single-responsibility loop.

I kept the logic contained in `BusinessDay` — the only class responsible for the rule — so `ResolveRegistrationDate` and the other pipeline steps that call it are unchanged. This mirrors the reference `toBusinessDay(...)` implementation already present in the acceptance test harness.

## Verification

`./mvnw test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` (the `AcceptanceTest` that asserts the default registration date always falls on a business day).
